skill.name: personal-finance-visualizer
skill.description: Turn user-provided personal finance records into a local interactive report with spending, income, transfers and cash movement in English or Chinese. Use for statement-based finance charts and period comparisons, not bank-account actions or investment advice.
skill.summary: Visualize authorized financial records locally with reconciled spending, income, transfers, and period comparisons.

content.user_title: Visualize Personal Finances in Local Reports
content.value_statement: Financial records can mix spending, transfers, refunds, and shared costs, making period totals difficult to interpret. This skill organizes authorized records into interactive local reports with separate financial views and transaction details.
actual_capabilities: Render normalized JSON or CSV as interactive overview, spending, income, and transfer views.
Compare day, week, month, and year periods within confirmed source coverage.
Apply confirmed personal expense shares, exact full-refund mappings, and partial transfer settlement allocations.
Inspect category and merchant charts with searchable transaction details.
Display the report interface in English or Simplified Chinese.
Serve reports from memory through a tokenized loopback URL or create an explicitly requested standalone HTML export.
limitations: Requires Python 3.10 or later, a modern browser, and normalized input; PDF extraction depends on separate authorized tools.
Each report supports one currency with two decimal places and performs no currency conversion.
CSV input cannot express refund or settlement mappings; partial refunds do not automatically reduce spending.
Local rendering does not eliminate agent-host retention; the skill does not connect bank accounts, execute payments, or provide investment advice.

use_cases.title: Review Household Spending
use_cases.description: Compare monthly living costs, subscriptions, and housing expenses using confirmed personal shares and category breakdowns.

use_cases.title: Separate Income From Transfers
use_cases.description: Review confirmed income separately from account movements, reimbursements, and unexplained receipts without treating every deposit as earnings.

use_cases.title: Explain Shared Costs and Repayments
use_cases.description: Inspect confirmed expense shares and loan repayments while keeping original transaction amounts and unresolved items visible.

prompt_templates.title: Preview a Fictional Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Open an English report using the fictional demo data. Do not read personal files or save an export.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: explore the report without supplying financial records.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Normalized CSV
prompt_templates.prompt: Use my supplied normalized CSV for [start date] through [end date] in [currency]. Show monthly spending locally. Flag unclear coverage or classifications.
prompt_templates.scenario: Basic: inspect an already normalized transaction export.

prompt_templates.title: Reconcile Shares and Refunds
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my authorized records for [period]. Confirm proposed personal shares and full-refund matches before applying them. Show spending and bank-date cash movement separately.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: account for shared purchases and confirmed refunds.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Reconciled Transfers
prompt_templates.prompt: Use my normalized JSON with confirmed transfer settlements. Compare quarterly months, preserve unresolved receipts as transfers, and show Chinese labels. Export only to [authorized absolute path].
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: compare reconciled periods and request a private local export.

output_examples.input: Illustrative USD records: salary 3,000, everyday expense 60, housing expense 1,000 at a confirmed 50% share, and internal savings transfer 200.
output: Personal spending: 560, including 500 for the confirmed housing share.
Income: 3,000. External outflow: 1,060. Net external movement: 1,940.
The internal savings movement is excluded from external cash movement; original transaction amounts remain available.

output_examples.input: Illustrative USD records: January purchase 84, confirmed full refund 84 in February, loan transfer 120, and confirmed repayment allocation 50.
output: The fully refunded purchase contributes no personal spending, while purchase and refund retain their original bank dates in cash movement.
The confirmed loan has 70 outstanding after the 50 repayment allocation.
Transaction details preserve original amounts and identify matched refunds and settled transfers.

output_examples.input: A Simplified Chinese report requested for normalized records covering March 10 through March 31.
output: A local interactive report opens with Chinese interface labels and coverage limited to the supplied dates.
Daily averages use the 22 covered calendar days rather than assuming a complete month.
Source notes retain unresolved classifications and coverage limitations.

best_practices: Confirm source coverage, amount signs, account ownership, and duplicate evidence before rendering; use account aliases instead of account numbers.
Apply shares, full-refund mappings, and transfer settlements only after confirmation; document unresolved items in report notes.
Pass newly normalized data through standard input, keep the report URL private, and export only to an explicitly authorized private destination.
anti_patterns: Treating every incoming payment as income or matching transactions solely by name, amount, or date.
Combining currencies, inventing exchange rates, or claiming complete coverage from partial account records.
Publishing reports, saving private screenshots, placing records in repositories, or assuming local rendering removes host retention.

faq.question: Which file formats are supported?
faq.answer: The renderer accepts normalized JSON and CSV. Bank exports need explicit field mapping. PDF extraction requires a separate authorized tool.

faq.question: Does the skill connect to my bank?
faq.answer: No. It uses authorized records you provide. It does not collect credentials, connect accounts, or execute payments.

faq.question: Does my financial data leave my computer?
faq.answer: The renderer makes no external requests. Your agent host may retain supplied data or tool transcripts, so cloud-agent processing is not fully offline.

faq.question: Can I save the report?
faq.answer: Yes, on explicit request. The standalone HTML embeds transaction data; choose a new private destination outside Git repositories and the installed skill.

faq.question: How are refunds and repayments handled?
faq.answer: Confirmed exact full refunds remove matched purchases from spending. Confirmed transfer allocations reduce adjusted transfers. Partial refunds remain separate; CSV cannot express these mappings.

faq.question: Which languages and currencies are supported?
faq.answer: The interface supports English and Simplified Chinese. Each report uses one currency with two decimal places, without currency conversion.
